runs.text: SUBSCRIPTION AGREEMENT
for
CLASS B COMMON UNITS
of
ASC SIMPHONIC II, LLC
(a Delaware limited liability company)

THE SECURITIES OFFERED HEREBY HAVE NOT BEEN REGISTERED UNDER THE U.S. SECURITIES ACT OF 1933, AS AMENDED (THE “SECURITIES ACT”), OR THE SECURITIES LAWS OF ANY STATE, AND ARE BEING OFFERED AND SOLD IN RELIANCE ON EXEMPTIONS FROM THE REGISTRATION REQUIREMENTS OF THE SECURITIES ACT AND APPLICABLE STATE SECURITIES LAWS. THE SECURITIES ARE BEING OFFERED ONLY TO PERSONS WHO QUALIFY AS “ACCREDITED INVESTORS” AS DEFINED IN RULE 501(a) OF REGULATION D PROMULGATED UNDER THE SECURITIES ACT.

THE SECURITIES MAY NOT BE OFFERED, SOLD, TRANSFERRED, PLEDGED, HYPOTHECATED, OR OTHERWISE DISPOSED OF EXCEPT IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE OPERATING AGREEMENT OF THE COMPANY AND APPLICABLE LAW. NO PUBLIC MARKET EXISTS OR IS EXPECTED TO DEVELOP FOR THE SECURITIES. INVESTORS MUST BE PREPARED TO BEAR THE ECONOMIC RISK OF THIS INVESTMENT FOR AN INDEFINITE PERIOD AND TO RISK A TOTAL LOSS OF THEIR INVESTMENT.

PRIOR TO EXECUTING THIS SUBSCRIPTION AGREEMENT, EACH PROSPECTIVE INVESTOR SHOULD CAREFULLY REVIEW THE CONFIDENTIAL PRIVATE PLACEMENT MEMORANDUM OF THE COMPANY DATED May 15, 2026 (THE “MEMORANDUM”) AND THE OPERATING AGREEMENT OF THE COMPANY (THE “OPERATING AGREEMENT”), AND CONSULT WITH SUCH INVESTOR’S OWN LEGAL, TAX, AND FINANCIAL ADVISORS.
INSTRUCTIONS TO PROSPECTIVE INVESTORS

In order to subscribe for Class B Common Units (the “Class B Units” or the “Securities”) of ASC Simphonic II, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the “Company”), each prospective investor (a “Subscriber”) must:

Review the Offering Documents. Read this Subscription Agreement, the Memorandum, and the Operating Agreement in their entirety, and consult with the Subscriber’s own legal, tax, and financial advisors.
Complete this Subscription Agreement. Complete and execute the signature pages to this Subscription Agreement, including the Subscription Amount and all other required information.
Complete the Accredited Investor Questionnaire. Complete and execute the Accredited Investor Questionnaire attached hereto as Exhibit A.
Execute the Operating Agreement Counterpart Signature Page. Complete and execute the counterpart signature page to the Operating Agreement attached hereto as Exhibit B.
Provide Identification and Anti-Money Laundering Documentation. Provide such identification and other anti-money laundering documentation as the Manager may reasonably request.
Submit Documents and Funds. Return all completed and executed documents and wire the Subscription Amount in accordance with the wire instructions provided by the Manager.

The Manager (as defined below) may, in its sole and absolute discretion, accept or reject any subscription, in whole or in part. A subscription is not binding on the Company until accepted by the Manager. If a subscription is rejected (or accepted only in part), the rejected portion of the Subscription Amount will be returned to the Subscriber without interest or deduction.
All inquiries should be directed to:
AltSpot Capital, LLC
as Manager of ASC Simphonic II, LLC
Attn: Ryan Billings
3101 Ocean Park Blvd, Santa Monica, CA 90405
Email: contact@thealtspot.com
SUBSCRIPTION AGREEMENT

This SUBSCRIPTION AGREEMENT (this “Subscription Agreement” or this “Agreement”) is entered into as of the date set forth on the signature page hereto (the “Subscription Date”), by and between ASC Simphonic II, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the “Company”), and the undersigned subscriber (the “Subscriber”).

Capitalized terms used and not otherwise defined in this Agreement shall have the meanings ascribed to such terms in the Memorandum or in the Operating Agreement of the Company, dated as of May 15, 2026 (as the same may be amended, supplemented, or restated from time to time, the “Operating Agreement”).

WHEREAS, the Company is a Delaware limited liability company formed for the sole purpose of acquiring and holding shares of Series Seed Preferred Stock (the “Series Seed Preferred”) of Simphonic, Inc., a Delaware corporation (“Simphonic”), together with associated warrants to purchase common stock of Simphonic (the “Warrants” and, together with the Series Seed Preferred, the “Portfolio Securities”);

WHEREAS, the Company is offering Class B Common Units (the “Class B Units” or the “Securities”) to a limited number of “accredited investors” as defined in Rule 501(a) of Regulation D promulgated under the Securities Act, in reliance on the exemption from registration provided by Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act and Rule 506 of Regulation D, and applicable state securities law exemptions (the “Offering”);
WHEREAS, AltSpot Capital, LLC serves as the Manager of the Company (the “Manager”); and

WHEREAS, the Subscriber wishes to subscribe for, and the Company wishes to issue and sell to the Subscriber, {{units}} Class B Units, on and subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement and the Operating Agreement.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the foregoing recitals and the mutual covenants and agreements contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows:

Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, the Subscriber hereby irrevocably subscribes for and agrees to purchase {{units}} Class B Units (the “Subscribed Units”) at a price of $1.00 per Class B Unit (the “Per-Unit Price”), for an aggregate subscription amount equal to the Per-Unit Price multiplied by the number of Subscribed Units (the “Subscription Amount”). The Subscription Amount must be at least $50,000 (the “Minimum Subscription Amount”), provided that the Manager may, in its sole and absolute discretion, accept a Subscription Amount in a lesser amount.

This Agreement does not constitute an offer to sell or a solicitation of an offer to buy. The Subscriber’s subscription is not binding on the Company until this Agreement is accepted (the date of acceptance, the “Closing Date”) by, or on behalf of, the Company by execution of the signature page hereto, and the Subscriber’s admission as a Member is conditioned on the Subscriber’s execution of the counterpart signature page to the Operating Agreement attached hereto as Exhibit B. The Manager may accept or reject this subscription, in whole or in part, in its sole and absolute discretion. If this subscription is rejected, in whole or in part, the rejected portion of the Subscription Amount shall be returned promptly to the Subscriber without interest or deduction, and this Agreement shall (with respect to the rejected portion) be null and void.

Concurrently with the delivery of this Agreement, or otherwise as instructed by the Manager, the Subscriber shall pay the Subscription Amount in immediately available funds by wire transfer to the account designated by the Manager. The Manager may hold subscription funds in a non-interest-bearing account pending acceptance of this Agreement and the closing of the Offering. No interest will accrue or be payable on any subscription funds held by or for the Company.

The Subscriber’s offer to purchase the Subscribed Units is irrevocable, and the Subscriber may not withdraw, cancel, or revoke this Agreement once delivered, except as may be required by applicable law.

blocks.title: Manager’s Right to Modify the Offering

runs.text: The Manager may, in its sole and absolute discretion: (a) modify, terminate, withdraw, or extend the Offering at any time; (b) conduct one or more closings of the Offering; (c) admit additional Members on such dates and on such terms as the Manager determines, subject to the Operating Agreement; and (d) waive or vary any of the conditions of the Offering with respect to one or more Subscribers.

The Subscriber acknowledges that the Company’s acquisition of the Portfolio Securities is conditioned upon, among other things, the satisfaction or waiver of the conditions to closing set forth in the definitive transaction documents to be entered into between the Company and Simphonic. If such acquisition does not occur, or if the Manager determines, in its sole discretion, not to proceed with such acquisition, the Manager will return uninvested subscription funds to Subscribers (less any actual Company expenses incurred to date, to the extent provided in the Operating Agreement) without interest or deduction.

articles.title: RECEIPT AND REVIEW OF OFFERING DOCUMENTS

runs.text: The Subscriber hereby acknowledges and represents that:

The Subscriber has received, carefully reviewed, and understands this Agreement, the Memorandum, the Operating Agreement, and any other materials provided by the Manager in connection with the Offering (collectively, the “Offering Documents”), including without limitation the risk factors, conflicts of interest, and tax considerations described therein;

The Subscriber has had the opportunity to ask questions of, and receive answers from, the Manager and its representatives concerning the terms and conditions of the Offering, the Company, Simphonic, and the Portfolio Securities, and to obtain such additional information as the Subscriber has deemed necessary to verify the accuracy of the information furnished;

In making the decision to subscribe for the Subscribed Units, the Subscriber has relied solely on the Offering Documents and the Subscriber’s own independent investigation, due diligence, and analysis (and that of the Subscriber’s own advisors), and has not relied on any oral or written representation made by the Company, the Manager, or any of their respective affiliates, employees, agents, or representatives that is not contained in this Agreement or in the other Offering Documents;

The Subscriber has been advised to, and has had the opportunity to, consult with the Subscriber’s own attorney, accountant, and other financial and tax advisors regarding this investment and the Offering Documents;

The Subscriber acknowledges that the Memorandum is a summary of certain matters and is qualified in its entirety by the Operating Agreement and other definitive documents; in the event of any inconsistency between the Memorandum and the Operating Agreement, the Operating Agreement shall control;

The Subscriber acknowledges that no person has been authorized to make any representation or to provide any information other than as set forth in the Offering Documents, and the Subscriber has not relied on any such other representation or information; and

The Subscriber understands that, except as expressly set forth in the Offering Documents, the Company has not made and is not making any representation or warranty regarding Simphonic, its business, prospects, financial condition, results of operations, or the Portfolio Securities, and that information regarding Simphonic in the Offering Documents has not been independently verified by the Company or the Manager.

articles.title: REPRESENTATIONS, WARRANTIES, AND COVENANTS OF THE SUBSCRIBER

runs.text: The Subscriber hereby represents, warrants, covenants, and agrees, as of the date hereof and as of the Closing Date (in each case as if made on and as of such date), as follows. These representations, warranties, and covenants are made in addition to (and not in limitation of) those set forth in Article 10 of the Operating Agreement, which the Subscriber will also make upon execution of the Operating Agreement counterpart signature page.

The Subscriber is an “accredited investor” as defined in Rule 501(a) of Regulation D promulgated under the Securities Act. The Subscriber’s accredited investor status is correctly indicated on the Accredited Investor Questionnaire attached hereto as Exhibit A, which is incorporated by reference into this Agreement and made a part hereof. All information provided by the Subscriber in the Accredited Investor Questionnaire is true, complete, and correct as of the date hereof and will be true, complete, and correct as of the Closing Date.

The Subscriber is acquiring the Subscribed Units solely for the Subscriber’s own account, for investment purposes only, and not with a view to, or for resale in connection with, any distribution thereof, in whole or in part, in violation of the Securities Act or any applicable state securities laws. The Subscriber has no present intention of selling, granting any participation in, or otherwise distributing the Subscribed Units. The Subscriber does not have any contract, undertaking, agreement, or arrangement with any person to sell, transfer, grant a participation in, or otherwise distribute the Subscribed Units.
The Subscriber understands that:

The Subscribed Units have not been, and will not be, registered under the Securities Act or qualified or registered under the securities laws of any state or other jurisdiction, in reliance on exemptions from such registration and qualification requirements, including the exemption provided by Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act and Rule 506 of Regulation D, and that the availability of such exemptions depends in part on the accuracy of the Subscriber’s representations herein;

The Subscribed Units constitute “restricted securities” within the meaning of Rule 144 under the Securities Act, and may not be resold, pledged, hypothecated, or otherwise transferred unless registered under the Securities Act and applicable state securities laws or pursuant to an available exemption from such registration and qualification requirements;

Neither the Company nor the Manager has any obligation to register or qualify the Subscribed Units under the Securities Act, any state securities laws, or any other law, or to assist the Subscriber in complying with any exemption from registration; and
The Subscribed Units may bear restrictive legends in accordance with the Operating Agreement and applicable law.

blocks.title: Knowledge and Experience; Ability to Bear Risk

runs.text: The Subscriber, alone or together with the Subscriber’s advisors who are unaffiliated with and not compensated, directly or indirectly, by the Company or the Manager, has such knowledge and experience in financial, tax, and business matters as to be capable of evaluating the merits and risks of an investment in the Company. The Subscriber has the financial ability to bear the economic risk of an investment in the Company for an indefinite period of time, has adequate means of providing for the Subscriber’s current needs and contingencies, has no need for liquidity with respect to the investment in the Company, and can afford a complete loss of the Subscriber’s investment.
The Subscriber acknowledges that:
An investment in the Subscribed Units is speculative and involves a high degree of risk, including the risk of total loss of the Subscriber’s investment;
The Company is a single-purpose investment vehicle whose sole investment will be in Simphonic, and accordingly the Subscriber will have no diversification within the Company;
The Company is newly organized and has no operating or financial history;

There is no public market for the Subscribed Units, and none is expected to develop, and the Subscribed Units are subject to substantial restrictions on transfer under the Operating Agreement, the Securities Act, and applicable state securities laws;

The Subscriber may be required, under certain circumstances described in the Operating Agreement (including Section 2.5), to make additional capital contributions to the Company, and a failure to do so may result in dilution of the Subscriber’s interest in the Company;

The Subscriber has carefully reviewed the risk factors set forth in the Memorandum, including but not limited to those relating to (a) the single-asset concentration in Simphonic, (b) the limited governance, voting, and information rights of Class B Members, (c) the limited fiduciary duties and broad indemnification of the Manager, (d) potential conflicts of interest involving the Manager and its affiliates (including ASC Simphonic LLC, an existing Series A holder of Simphonic), (e) the contingent and capped nature of the Revenue Participation Rights, (f) the time-limited nature of the Warrants, (g) U.S. federal, state, and local tax matters, including the Company’s intended election under Section 6226 of the Code (push-out election) and the Subscriber’s indemnification obligations under Section 7.4 of the Operating Agreement, (h) the early-stage nature of Simphonic and the healthcare regulatory and AI-related risks affecting Simphonic’s business, and (i) the mandatory binding arbitration in Los Angeles, California; and
The Subscriber has carefully evaluated such risk factors and is willing and able to bear the economic risks of, and a complete loss of, the Subscriber’s investment.

The Subscriber, if a natural person, has reached the age of majority in the Subscriber’s jurisdiction of residence and has full power and legal capacity to execute this Agreement, the Accredited Investor Questionnaire, and the counterpart signature page to the Operating Agreement, and to perform the Subscriber’s obligations hereunder and thereunder. The Subscriber, if not a natural person, is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of its jurisdiction of formation, has full power and authority to execute and deliver this Agreement, the Accredited Investor Questionnaire, and the Operating Agreement, and to perform its obligations hereunder and thereunder, and has duly taken all action necessary to authorize such execution, delivery, and performance. The execution and delivery by the Subscriber of, and performance by the Subscriber of its obligations under, this Agreement, the Accredited Investor Questionnaire, and the Operating Agreement do not and will not (a) violate any law, regulation, judgment, or order applicable to the Subscriber, (b) violate or conflict with the Subscriber’s organizational documents (if applicable), or (c) violate, conflict with, result in a breach of, or constitute a default under any agreement to which the Subscriber is a party or by which the Subscriber is bound.

This Agreement, the Accredited Investor Questionnaire, and the Operating Agreement, when executed and delivered by the Subscriber, will constitute the legal, valid, and binding obligations of the Subscriber, enforceable against the Subscriber in accordance with their respective terms, except as enforceability may be limited by bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, or similar laws affecting creditors’ rights generally and by general equitable principles.

The Subscription Amount and any subsequent capital contributions to be made by the Subscriber are derived from sources that are lawful and have not been derived directly or indirectly from any activity that contravenes any applicable laws or regulations, including any laws or regulations relating to anti-money laundering, anti-terrorism, anti-bribery and corruption, or sanctions. The Subscriber is not, nor is any beneficial owner, controlling person, principal, or affiliate of the Subscriber, (a) a person or entity named on the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List or any other sanctions list maintained by the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (“OFAC”), or (b) a person or entity organized or resident in any country or territory that is the subject of comprehensive sanctions administered by OFAC. The Subscriber agrees to provide such additional information and documentation as the Manager may reasonably request to comply with anti-money laundering, anti-terrorism, sanctions, and other similar laws and regulations.

The Subscriber acknowledges that the Offering is being conducted in reliance on Rule 506(c) of Regulation D under the Securities Act and that the Company is required to take reasonable steps to verify the Subscriber’s status as an accredited investor. The Subscriber agrees to (a) complete accredited investor verification through iCapital (formerly Parallel Markets) or such other third-party verification service as the Manager may designate (the “Verification Service”), or (b) at the Manager’s option, deliver to the Manager a written confirmation, dated within the prior three (3) months, from a registered broker-dealer, registered investment adviser, licensed attorney, or certified public accountant, stating that such person has taken reasonable steps to verify the Subscriber’s accredited investor status and has determined that the Subscriber is an accredited investor. The Subscriber authorizes the Verification Service to share the results of such verification with the Manager and the Company, and the Subscriber agrees to provide such additional information and documentation as the Verification Service or the Manager may reasonably request to complete the verification. The Subscriber acknowledges that the Manager may decline to accept the Subscriber’s subscription if accredited investor status cannot be verified to the Manager’s reasonable satisfaction in accordance with Rule 506(c).

Either (a) the Subscriber has a preexisting personal or business relationship with the Company, the Manager, or one or more of the Manager’s control persons, or (b) by reason of the Subscriber’s business or financial experience (or that of the Subscriber’s financial advisor who is unaffiliated with, and not compensated by, the Company or the Manager), the Subscriber is capable of evaluating the risks and merits of an investment in the Subscribed Units and of protecting the Subscriber’s own interests in connection with this investment.
The Subscriber understands that:
The U.S. federal, state, local, and non-U.S. tax consequences of an investment in the Company are complex and uncertain;

The Company will be classified as a partnership for U.S. federal income tax purposes, and the Subscriber will be required to take into account the Subscriber’s allocable share of the Company’s items of income, gain, loss, deduction, and credit, regardless of whether the Company makes any distributions in any particular year;

The Company intends to elect the application of Section 6226 of the Code (push-out election), as set forth in Section 7.4 of the Operating Agreement, and accordingly any IRS adjustments to the Company’s items of income or deduction may be allocated to the Subscriber for the reviewed year;

Pursuant to Section 7.4 of the Operating Agreement, the Subscriber is required to provide the Tax Representative with such tax information, documents, certifications, tax identification numbers, and tax forms as the Tax Representative may request, and to indemnify the Company, the Manager, and the Tax Representative against tax liabilities resulting from the Subscriber’s failure to comply;
The Subscriber will be responsible for the Subscriber’s own tax liabilities (subject to any Tax Distributions under Section 5.6 of the Operating Agreement);

None of the Company, the Manager, the other Members, nor their respective affiliates, employees, agents, or representatives will be responsible or liable for the tax consequences to the Subscriber of an investment in the Company;
The Subscriber is relying solely on the Subscriber’s own advisors with respect to the tax consequences of this investment; and

The Subscriber acknowledges that there can be no assurance that the Code or the Treasury Regulations will not be amended or interpreted in the future in a manner that adversely affects the Subscriber.

The Subscriber represents and warrants that the Subscriber is, or is not, a “benefit plan investor” within the meaning of Section 3(42) of ERISA and the U.S. Department of Labor’s plan asset regulations (a “Benefit Plan Investor”), as indicated by the Subscriber’s response on the Accredited Investor Questionnaire. If the Subscriber is a Benefit Plan Investor, the Subscriber further represents and warrants that the Subscriber’s investment in the Company has been duly authorized and is in compliance with all applicable provisions of ERISA and the Code, and that the fiduciary causing the Subscriber to make this investment has determined that the investment is appropriate for the Benefit Plan Investor.

The Subscriber acknowledges that the Memorandum and the other Offering Documents have been furnished to the Subscriber on a confidential basis. The Subscriber will not, without the prior written consent of the Manager, reproduce, distribute, disclose, or use the Memorandum or any other Offering Document, or any portion thereof or information contained therein, except that the Subscriber may disclose such information (a) to the Subscriber’s legal, tax, financial, and other professional advisors who have a need to know such information for the purpose of evaluating the Subscriber’s investment and who are bound by obligations of confidentiality, and (b) as required by applicable law, regulation, or legal process, in which case the Subscriber will, to the extent legally permissible, promptly notify the Manager prior to disclosure.

The Subscriber will promptly notify the Manager in writing if any of the representations or warranties made by the Subscriber in this Agreement or in the Accredited Investor Questionnaire becomes inaccurate or incomplete in any material respect at any time prior to the Closing Date or thereafter. Until expressly notified by the Subscriber to the contrary, the Manager and the Company may rely on the representations, warranties, and information provided by the Subscriber as continuing to be true, complete, and correct.

All representations, warranties, covenants, and agreements made by the Subscriber in this Agreement, the Accredited Investor Questionnaire, and the Operating Agreement shall survive the execution and delivery of this Agreement, the acceptance of the Subscriber’s subscription, the Closing Date, and the dissolution of the Company.

By executing this Agreement and the counterpart signature page to the Operating Agreement attached hereto as Exhibit B, the Subscriber agrees to become a Member of the Company, to be bound by all of the terms and conditions of the Operating Agreement, and to make the representations, warranties, and covenants set forth in Article 10 of the Operating Agreement. Upon acceptance of this Agreement by the Manager and execution by the Manager of the counterpart signature page to the Operating Agreement, the Subscriber shall be admitted as a Member of the Company holding {{units}} Class B Units, and Exhibit A to the Operating Agreement shall be amended to reflect the Subscriber’s admission, capital contribution, and Percentage Interest.

The Subscriber hereby irrevocably constitutes and appoints the Manager (and each authorized officer, agent, or attorney-in-fact thereof) as the Subscriber’s true and lawful attorney-in-fact, with full power of substitution and resubstitution, in the Subscriber’s name, place, and stead, to make, execute, sign, acknowledge, swear to, deliver, file, and record (a) the Operating Agreement (and any amendments and restatements thereto effected in accordance with its terms), (b) any amendments to Exhibit A or Schedule I to the Operating Agreement to reflect the admission, withdrawal, capital contribution, distribution, or Percentage Interest of any Member (including the Subscriber), (c) all certificates and other instruments deemed advisable by the Manager to qualify or continue the Company as a limited liability company in any jurisdiction in which the Company conducts business, (d) all instruments that effect a change or modification of the Company in accordance with the Operating Agreement, and (e) all instruments necessary or appropriate to dissolve and liquidate the Company in accordance with the Operating Agreement. This power of attorney is coupled with an interest, is irrevocable, and shall survive the death, incapacity, dissolution, bankruptcy, or disability of the Subscriber.

The Subscriber acknowledges and agrees that the Manager has full, complete, and exclusive authority, power, and discretion to manage and control the business, property, and affairs of the Company in accordance with the Operating Agreement, including with respect to (a) the negotiation, execution, and performance of the definitive transaction documents with Simphonic, (b) the voting, sale, exercise, and other disposition of the Portfolio Securities (including the Warrants), (c) responses to drag-along, tag-along, pre-emptive, right-of-first-refusal, and other similar provisions in Simphonic’s organizational documents and shareholder agreements, (d) tax matters and elections, including elections under Sections 6221(b) and 6226 of the Code, (e) capital calls, distributions, and admission of additional Members, and (f) all other matters relating to the operation of the Company. The Subscriber further acknowledges that, except as expressly provided in the Operating Agreement, Class B Units have no voting rights and Class B Members have no right to participate in management of the Company.

The Subscriber agrees to indemnify and hold harmless the Company, the Manager, and each of their respective members, managers, officers, directors, employees, agents, affiliates, advisors, and representatives (each, an “Indemnified Party”) from and against any and all losses, claims, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys’ fees and disbursements) arising out of or relating to:
Any breach by the Subscriber of any representation, warranty, covenant, or agreement made by the Subscriber in this Agreement, the Accredited Investor Questionnaire, or the Operating Agreement;
Any inaccuracy or omission in any information provided by the Subscriber to the Company or the Manager;
Any disposition of any Subscribed Units by the Subscriber in violation of this Agreement, the Operating Agreement, or applicable law; and

Any tax liabilities of the Company arising as a result of the Subscriber’s failure to comply with Sections 7.4.2 and 7.4.3 of the Operating Agreement (including failure to provide tax information requested by the Tax Representative or to report adjustments allocated to the Subscriber under Section 6226 of the Code).

The Subscriber’s indemnification obligations under this Section 5 shall be in addition to, and not in limitation of, the Subscriber’s indemnification obligations under the Operating Agreement (including under Section 7.4 thereof) and shall survive the dissolution of the Company and any transfer or assignment of the Subscriber’s Units.

This Agreement shall be governed by, and construed and enforced in accordance with, the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to any conflicts-of-laws principles that would require the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction.

Any controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement (other than any claim for which equitable relief is sought to enforce the confidentiality, transfer, or similar provisions of this Agreement or the Operating Agreement) shall be resolved by binding, non-appealable arbitration before the American Arbitration Association in Los Angeles, California, in accordance with Section 11.4 of the Operating Agreement. THE SUBSCRIBER HEREBY KNOWINGLY, VOLUNTARILY, AND INTENTIONALLY WAIVES, TO THE FULLEST EXTENT PERMITTED BY LAW, ANY RIGHT THE SUBSCRIBER MAY HAVE TO A TRIAL BY JURY IN RESPECT OF ANY LITIGATION ARISING OUT OF, UNDER, OR IN CONNECTION WITH THIS AGREEMENT.

All notices, requests, demands, and other communications under this Agreement shall be in writing (including by electronic mail) and shall be deemed to have been duly given and received when delivered to the address or email address specified by the recipient on the signature page hereto (or as otherwise designated by the recipient by notice given in accordance with this Section 6.3).

This Agreement (including the Exhibits hereto), together with the Operating Agreement, constitutes the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior agreements, understandings, negotiations, and discussions, whether oral or written, with respect to such subject matter. To the extent any provision of this Agreement conflicts with any provision of the Operating Agreement, the Operating Agreement shall control.
This Agreement may not be amended, modified, or supplemented except by a written instrument signed by each of the parties hereto.

This Agreement may not be assigned by the Subscriber without the prior written consent of the Manager, which consent may be granted or withheld in the Manager’s sole and absolute discretion. Any purported assignment in violation of this Section 6.6 shall be null and void. Subject to the foregoing, this Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties hereto and their respective successors, heirs, executors, administrators, legal representatives, and permitted assigns.

Except as expressly set forth herein with respect to Indemnified Parties, this Agreement is for the sole benefit of the parties hereto and their respective successors and permitted assigns, and nothing herein, express or implied, is intended to or shall confer upon any other person any legal or equitable right, benefit, or remedy of any nature whatsoever under or by reason of this Agreement.

If any provision of this Agreement is held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable in any jurisdiction, such invalidity, illegality, or unenforceability shall not affect any other provision of this Agreement or invalidate or render unenforceable such provision in any other jurisdiction, and this Agreement shall be reformed, construed, and enforced in such jurisdiction so as to best give effect to the parties’ intent.

This Agreement may be executed in two or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Counterparts may be delivered by facsimile, electronic mail (including PDF or other imaged file), or other electronic means (including DocuSign or any other electronic signature method that complies with the U.S. federal ESIGN Act of 2000), and a counterpart so delivered shall be deemed valid, binding, and effective for all purposes.
The headings of the sections of this Agreement are for convenience of reference only and shall not affect the interpretation or construction of any provision of this Agreement.

This Agreement has been negotiated by the parties with the advice of counsel and shall not be construed against the drafter. Each reference to “including” shall be deemed to mean “including without limitation.” Each reference to a particular gender shall be deemed to include each other gender, and each reference to the singular shall be deemed to include the plural and vice versa.

The Subscriber agrees to execute and deliver such additional documents, instruments, and certificates, and to take such additional actions, as the Manager may reasonably request in order to give effect to the provisions of this Agreement and to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby.

ACCREDITED INVESTOR QUESTIONNAIRE
Purpose of Questionnaire

This Accredited Investor Questionnaire (this “Questionnaire”) is being furnished to you in connection with the offer and sale by ASC Simphonic II, LLC (the “Company”) of Class B Common Units (the “Securities”) to qualify the offer and sale of the Securities for an exemption from registration under the U.S. Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “Securities Act”), pursuant to Section 4(a)(2) thereof and Rule 506 of Regulation D promulgated thereunder, and from registration under applicable state securities laws.

To establish the availability of these exemptions, the Company is required to confirm that each prospective investor is an “accredited investor” within the meaning of Rule 501(a) of Regulation D under the Securities Act. Your responses to this Questionnaire will be relied upon for purposes of confirming your accredited investor status. A. Natural Persons
If the Subscriber is a natural person (or a natural person and the Subscriber’s spouse, jointly), the Subscriber qualifies as an accredited investor if any of the following is true:

[ ](1) Net Worth Test. The Subscriber’s individual net worth, or joint net worth with the Subscriber’s spouse or spousal equivalent, exceeds $1,000,000 at the time of subscription. For purposes of this calculation, (a) “spousal equivalent” means a cohabitant occupying a relationship generally equivalent to that of a spouse; (b) the value of the Subscriber’s primary residence is not included in the calculation of net worth, and indebtedness secured by the primary residence (up to its estimated fair market value) is not included as a liability, except that any incremental amount of indebtedness incurred in the 60 days preceding subscription (other than as a result of the acquisition of the primary residence) is included as a liability, and any indebtedness in excess of the fair market value of the primary residence is included as a liability.

[ ](2) Income Test. The Subscriber had individual income in excess of $200,000 in each of the two most recent calendar years (or joint income with the Subscriber’s spouse or spousal equivalent in excess of $300,000 in each of those years), and reasonably expects to reach the same income level in the current calendar year.

[ ](3) Professional Certifications.
